summary:
Astrophage is an operational Earth observation and disaster sentinel built around the NASA–ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar (NISAR) mission to transform raw radar interferograms into intuitive planetary protection. 

Optical satellites are blind through cloud cover, smoke, and nighttime darkness. While NISAR’s dual-frequency L-band radar penetrates weather and vegetation canopy, raw radar interferograms exist as multi-gigabyte complex phase files inaccessible to disaster managers. Astrophage solves this bottleneck.

The platform continuously fuses global hazard feeds (USGS earthquakes, NASA EONET events, GDACS tropical cyclones, Smithsonian volcanic alerts) with real-time NISAR orbit tracks from CelesTrak. Querying NASA’s Common Metadata Repository (CMR/ASF DAAC), Astrophage identifies matching radar granules and automatically unwraps real NISAR L2 GUNW interferograms to drape true millimeter-scale ground displacement directly onto 3D elevation terrain. 

With automated 10-minute edge watchlists and email alerts, Astrophage empowers emergency responders, civil engineers, and coastal cities to detect subtle fault creep, volcanic inflation, and subsidence before catastrophic collapse occurs.
details:
1. WHAT EXACTLY DOES IT DO & WHAT CHALLENGE DOES IT ANSWER?


Astrophage addresses the NASA Space Apps Challenge "Dancing with the SARs" by transforming raw Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) data into actionable disaster intelligence.

While optical satellites cannot penetrate clouds, smoke, or night, NISAR's L-band radar observes the Earth surface in all weather conditions. However, raw radar interferograms are complex, multi-gigabyte HDF5 phase files requiring specialized scientific software (e.g., ISCE3) and hours of processing. Astrophage eliminates this barrier: it continuously monitors planetary hazards, matches them with authentic NASA NISAR radar granules, and renders validated millimeter ground displacement on interactive 3D terrain.

2. HOW DOES IT WORK? (THE FOUR OBSERVATORY MODALITIES)

Astrophage is structured around an integrated mission-control Observatory:

• 2D Tactical Vector Radar (EventRadar2D):

Built using MapLibre GL and deck.gl with bundled Natural Earth vector geometry for zero-latency, offline-capable mapping. It renders live seismic clusters, volcanic activity, and cyclone tracks. Users can search any global city, lock on with a targeted Radar Reticle, view local NISAR track swaths, and scrub multi-temporal 12-day repeat cycles.

• Authentic NASA NISAR Granule Matching:

Astrophage queries NASA's Common Metadata Repository (CMR/ASF DAAC) for real NISAR data collections (GUNW, GOFF, RUNW, RIFG). It calculates spatial polygon intersections and temporal baselines to identify pre- and post-event radar pairs that bracket an event date.

• 3D Topographic Strain Visualizer (3D Topo):

Our automated Python pipeline (tools/nisar-grid) downloads NASA NISAR L2 GUNW interferograms from ASF DAAC, unwraps line-of-sight (LOS) phase, removes noise and water decorrelation (coherence > 0.3), and drapes true millimeter surface motion onto real 3D elevation terrain (AWS Terrain Tiles/Three.js). Users can rotate the 3D terrain to probe point-by-point elevation, displacement in cm, and radar coherence.

• Automated Edge Sentinel:

A Cloudflare D1 serverless database running automated 10-minute cron triggers checks incoming feeds against custom user Watchlists, automatically dispatching alert emails via Resend when ground motion or tropical cyclones threaten watched areas.

3. SCIENTIFIC INTEGRITY: MEASURED VS. MODELLED

Astrophage maintains strict transparency:

- Earthquake (USGS), volcano (Smithsonian GVP), and cyclone (GDACS) records are real-time, unedited telemetry.

- Where an interferogram has been processed, ground motion is clearly badged in green as "NISAR MEASURED". Where an interferogram is not yet processed, displacement is transparently labelled "MODELLED" using empirical seismological moment equations (Wells & Coppersmith 1994; Hanks & Kanamori).

4. WHAT BENEFITS & INTENDED IMPACT DOES IT HAVE?

• For Emergency Responders: Immediate situational awareness showing exactly where and by how many millimeters the ground has ruptured or shifted following an earthquake.

• For Civil Engineers & Coastal Cities: Early detection of slow fault creep, levee deformation, and groundwater subsidence before structural failure.

• For Open Science: Democratizes NASA's most sophisticated radar mission so non-specialists can explore and export scientific dossiers in GeoJSON or CSV.

5. TOOLS, CODING LANGUAGES & TECHNOLOGIES USED

• Frontend: Next.js 16 (App Router), React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS v4, Zustand

• Visualization: Three.js, React Three Fiber, MapLibre GL, Deck.gl

• Radar Ingestion: Python (h5py, numpy, scipy, rasterio) for processing HDF5 GUNW files

• Backend & Infrastructure: Cloudflare Workers edge runtime, Cloudflare D1 (SQLite at the edge), OpenNext, Resend (email API)

• Quality & Testing: Vitest test suite (25+ test suites) running in GitHub Actions CI

6. WHAT WE HOPE TO ACHIEVE NEXT

• Serverless On-Demand Processing: Scale the Python unwrapping service into automated serverless containers to process GUNW files within minutes of an M5.0+ earthquake alert.

• Multi-temporal InSAR Time-Series: Integrate SBAS (Small Baseline Subset) algorithms to track long-term millimeter subsidence across critical infrastructure like bridges and dams.
